name_ru: Да И Лун Чжу Юань Ча
processing: Details of this blend are not well documented; ripe pu-erh from Menghai is typically Yunnan large-leaf sun-dried tea that is wet-piled, dried and pressed.
harvest_season: Not documented for this tea; factory ripe blends are generally not tied to a single picking.
appearance_dry: A round pressed cake is implied by the word yuancha; expect the dark, reddish-brown leaf typical of Menghai ripe tea.

appearance_wet: Typical of ripe pu-erh: soft, dark brown leaf.
taste_profile: No reliable tasting notes for this tea; ripe Menghai blends usually run smooth, earthy and sweet.

description:
Long Zhu, or Dragon Pillar, is a Dayi product name, listed here as a ripe pu-erh from Menghai. Chinese buyers mention a related 'little dragon pillar', but little else is documented about the tea.

Its recipe and leaf grade are not publicly set out. Assume only what is typical of its class: Yunnan large-leaf tea, wet-piled and pressed.

Brew it like other ripe Menghai tea, with a quick rinse, water near the boil and short early steeps. Judge it by your own cup.

When buying, confirm the exact name and weight on the wrapper, and check the batch and production date.
history: Little is documented about when this tea first appeared or how it has changed. No first release year can be confirmed.
